subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Generic MSVC runtime object lifecycle and UI control objects: scalar-deleting destructor stubs, shared vtable-reset cleanup fragments, linked-list owners and traversals, UI dispatch/validation controls, scroll and list-layout containers, text edit buffers, and a collision-system helper cluster sharing global dword_8AB6EC. Boundaries are pattern-based DERIVED proposals; most object identities are UNKNOWN.

summary: This packet groups generic runtime objects evidenced only by validated function IR. The dominant pattern is the MSVC scalar-deleting destructor: write the object vtable into this+0, run a common cleanup fragment (usually InitWithVTableCleanup 0x00487250, which itself writes vtable off_5AB968 and delegates to the shared helper sub_485EB0), then free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when the low bit of the flag argument is set. Eleven such stubs (0x00485510, 0x004855A0, 0x004855D0, 0x00485600, 0x00485630, 0x00485660, 0x004856F0, 0x00485A70, 0x00485B20, 0x00487690, 0x00487F10) plus the three vtable-reset fragments (0x00487250, 0x00487F30, 0x00488B30) are grouped as a pattern family, with the caveat that each installs a distinct vtable constant and grouping is not common-ownership proof. A second family is the UI dispatch/validation control: handlers validate the current value (UIValueValidator), set handler state via sub_487260, handle radio/check changes, perform a secondary validation through vtable slot +0x98, and finalize via sub_486600 (0x00487530, 0x004879E0, 0x00487E10, plus the toggle helper 0x00487D70 and state predicates 0x00487720/0x00487740). A third cluster operates on linked lists: node-freeing destructor 0x004859D0 and two traversals (0x00486600 head +0xCC, 0x00486630 head +0xD0) that call sub_49A5D0 per node. UI layout objects cover scroll clamping (0x00488970, setter 0x00488BC0) and screen-coordinate to list-index conversion (0x00489F40). Text-edit widgets initialize their buffer and flags (0x0048B4F0, 0x0048B7E0). A collision-system cluster shares global dword_8AB6EC (0x0047C940 difference-from-average, 0x0047C9D0 thunk to RangeWidthGetter, 0x0047CA30 timer dispatch into CollisionSystemInit). 0x0047C910 is a standalone constructor installing vtable off_5A6A68. 0x0047EE5C is a free-standing data-block init with no recorded callers. Compatibility contracts capture the scalar-deleting ABI, the dword_8AB6EC protocol, the vtable-slot layout used by UI dispatch, the text-edit buffer layout, and the list-index formula.

function_roles.role: UI object constructor: calls base UI constructor UIConstructorWithVTableParams, zeroes field +0xFC, installs vtable off_5A6A68, returns this.
Compute float difference: run shared Delegation step on global dword_8AB6EC, then return the caller's double truncated to float minus the lifetime average read by VehicleLifetimeAverageAccessor.
Thunk: forwards the address of global dword_8AB6EC to RangeWidthGetter as its single argument; invoked by CollisionSystemInit during collision-system setup.
Timer-based float dispatch: compute float via ShortComputation_89d0, pass it to CollisionSystemInit, return 0.

Init from data block: copy 36 bytes from global unk_7D0A30, format the integer via '%d' through the buffer-overflow-checked formatter, conditionally dispatch the formatted buffer via ConditionalCallWrapper, return 0.

Scalar-deleting destructor: reset vtable to off_5A6E70, free three non-null buffer pointers at +0x219C/+0x2194/+0x218C via FreeWrapper_7bcf, chain to base destructor sub_495300 and return its result; the object teardown path invoked by SimpleGetter.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AB4A0): write vtable, run common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flag bit 0 set, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AB290): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AB1E0): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AB130): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AB080): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5AAFD0): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor (vtable off_5A9660): write vtable, common cleanup via InitWithVTableCleanup, conditional free, return this.

Complex destructor: walk linked list rooted at +0x164 freeing each node data (when node flag byte at +0x8 non-zero) and each node, clear list fields +0x164/+0x168/+0x16C/+0x170, free standalone buffer +0x15C when non-null, run ConditionalDualCleanup on sub-objects +0x11C and +0xE0, chain to base destructor sub_485EB0, and free this when flag bit 0 set.
Scalar-deleting destructor wrapper: run object teardown via ShortComputation_6140, then free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flag bit 0 set, return this.
Scalar-deleting destructor: free sub-resources at +0x17C and +0x174 when non-null, run common cleanup FunctionCallWrapper_9440, free this when flag bit 0 set, return this.
List traversal: iterate singly linked list with head this[51] at +0xCC, advancing via node next pointer at node offset +0x18, invoking sub_49A5D0 once per node; returns 0.
List traversal: iterate linked list with head this[52] at +0xD0, advancing via node next pointer at node offset +0x18, invoking sub_49A5D0 once per node; returns 0.

Guarded conditional rectangle render: when enable flag set and sub-renderer pointer at +0x98 non-null, dispatch four bounds from +0x4/+0x8/+0xC/+0x10 to GuardedSubRectangleRenderDispatch; otherwise return the this pointer byte.

Indexed offset-pair lookup: guard against boundary from ShortComputation_adb0 with flag at +0xC8, fetch pair via LinkedListIndexedFieldReader, write combined offsets this[3]+v7 and this[1]+v8; returns 0 on guard/reader failure, 1 on success.
Vtable-reset-before-cleanup fragment: write vtable off_5AB968 into this+0 then delegate to shared cleanup helper sub_485EB0; used on both construction and destruction paths.

Validated UI dispatch: primary validation via UIValueValidator, set handler state via sub_487260(this,1), handle radio/check state via UIRadioCheckStateChangeHandler, secondary validation through vtable slot +0x98, finalize via sub_486600; returns -1 on any failure, 0 on success.
Scalar-deleting destructor: run sub-computation ShortComputation_76b0 on the object, then free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flag bit 0 set, return this.
Pure predicate over ShortComputation_6720 result: true when the callee result is 1 or 3.
Range check: true when ShortComputation_6720 result lies in the inclusive range [2, 3].

Validated UI dispatch init: primary validation via UIValueValidator, state-dependent vtable dispatch StateDependentVTableDispatch_7760(this,1), propagate control state change via UIControlStateChangeHandler, secondary validation through vtable slot +0x98, finalize via sub_486600; returns -1 on failure, 0 on success.

Pointer-based state toggle: retrieve child via vtable slot +0xAC (short-circuit through +0x38 with argument 1 when null), clear via +0x38 with argument 0, compute toggle value from child first dword inverted by flag +0xE4, set state via sub_487260 on change and notify via vtable slot +0x2C with argument 1.

Validated dispatch with value toggle: primary validation via UIValueValidator, set handler state via sub_487260, radio/check handling via UIRadioCheckStateChangeHandler, obtain value pointer through vtable slot +0xAC and toggle it (0<->1) when non-null, secondary validation through vtable slot +0x98, finalize via sub_486600; returns -1 on failure, 0 on success.
Scalar-deleting destructor: perform base vtable cleanup via VTableSetCleanup, then free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flag bit 0 set, return this.
Vtable-reset-before-cleanup fragment: write vtable off_5ABAC8 into this+0 then delegate to shared cleanup helper sub_485EB0 on a destruction path.

Clamp scroll offset at +0xE0: reset to 0 when negative, else clamp so offset + position (vtable slot +0x18) stays within extent (vtable slot +0x20); tail-call the accessor at vtable slot +0xA8 and return its result.
Vtable-reset fragment: write vtable off_5ABC28 into this+0 then delegate to shared helper sub_485EB0 for further initialization or teardown.
Trivial setter: store argument a2 into DWORD at offset +0xE0 and return a2; used by ConstructorDualSubInit as a field writer.

Convert screen y-coordinate to list item index from layout fields: trunc((a2 - 0x13C - 0x134 - 0x4) / 0x158) + 0x14C via CRTFtol, clamped within scroll and (when a3 set) visible-page and total-count bounds; returns -1 when item height not positive or y outside the vertical range.

Initialize edit-box fields: clear string buffer first byte (+0x2F0), point cursor +0x2F4 at buffer start, buffer size +0x2F8=256, char limit +0x300=16, length +0x2E8=0, and set byte flags +0xE0..0xE5, +0x1E7, +0x2EC; returns 0.

Text edit buffer init: store buffer pointer into +0x2F0 and size into +0x2F8, then call virtual slot at vtable+168 (0xA8) with argument 1; guarded on non-null pointer and positive size; returns 0. Called by UITextFieldInitialization.
Forwarding shim: read DWORD at offset +0x0, return result of widget-visibility toggle called with (*this, a2, this, a2); used by UIEventShortcutHandler and UIActiveStateToggle.
Active-focus wrapper: toggle active/focused state via UIActiveStateToggle, then dispatch the virtual method at vtable entry offset 0xAC on this; returns 0.

classes.name: CollisionSystemObject
classes.responsibility: Cluster of collision-system helpers sharing the global dword_8AB6EC: difference-from-lifetime-average computation, a thunk forwarding the global address to RangeWidthGetter, and a timer-based float dispatch into collision-system initialization. Grouping is pattern-based (shared global and adjacent addresses); object ownership is UNKNOWN.

classes.name: UIObjectBase
classes.responsibility: Constructor-only fragment: calls the base UI constructor, zeroes a field at +0xFC, and installs vtable off_5A6A68. Class identity UNKNOWN; the +0xFC field semantics (dispatch mode/state) are unproven.

classes.name: BufferResourceObject
classes.responsibility: Object holding three buffer pointers at +0x218C/+0x2194/+0x219C with vtable off_5A6E70; its destructor frees each non-null buffer then chains to base destructor sub_495300. Class identity UNKNOWN (existing analysis hints screen-data texture manager, unverified).

classes.name: VTableCleanupInitFragment
classes.responsibility: Three vtable-reset-before-cleanup fragments, each installing a distinct vtable (off_5AB968, off_5ABAC8, off_5ABC28) into this+0 then delegating to the shared cleanup helper sub_485EB0. Appear on both construction and destruction paths; each fragment belongs to its own object and grouping is pattern-based.

classes.name: ScalarDeletingObject
classes.responsibility: Group of MSVC scalar-deleting-destructor stubs: install the object vtable at this+0, run a common cleanup (usually InitWithVTableCleanup 0x00487250, sometimes a sub-computation such as ShortComputation_6140/ShortComputation_76b0/VTableSetCleanup), then free this via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flag bit 0 is set, returning this. Each method installs a distinct vtable; grouping is pattern-based and is NOT proof of common ownership.

classes.name: ListBufferDestroyer
classes.responsibility: Destructor of an object owning a singly linked list (head at +0x164; node data pointer at node+0x0, next at node+0x4, flag byte at node+0x8), a standalone buffer at +0x15C, and two sub-objects at +0x11C and +0xE0; it frees the nodes and buffer, clears the list fields, cleans the sub-objects via ConditionalDualCleanup, chains to base destructor sub_485EB0, and conditionally frees itself.

classes.name: LinkedListCallbackTraverser
classes.responsibility: Object exposing one or more linked lists whose nodes carry a next pointer at +0x18; traverses the list calling sub_49A5D0 once per node. One traversal reads its head at +0xCC, the other at +0xD0; these may be two lists on one object or two objects, and the extractor renders the node base as *(this+0xE4) and *(this+0xE8) respectively.

classes.name: UIConditionalRenderWidget
classes.responsibility: UI widget that conditionally renders a rectangle through a sub-renderer pointer when an enable flag is set: rectangle bounds stored at +0x4/+0x8/+0xC/+0x10 and sub-renderer pointer at +0x98 are dispatched to GuardedSubRectangleRenderDispatch.

classes.name: UIOffsetLookupTable
classes.responsibility: Indexed offset-pair lookup table used by UI rendering helpers (rectangle drawing and text-box scrollbar rendering): returns two combined offsets derived from base offsets +0x4 and +0xC plus indexed values fetched through LinkedListIndexedFieldReader, guarded by a boundary helper and a flag at +0xC8.

classes.name: UIValidatedDispatchControl
classes.responsibility: UI control dispatch handlers: validate the current value via UIValueValidator, set handler state via sub_487260, handle radio/check changes, perform a secondary validation through vtable slot +0x98, and finalize via sub_486600. Includes state predicates over ShortComputation_6720 (accepting result 1 or 3; range [2,3]) and a pointer-based state toggle that reads a child through vtable slot +0xAC, sets/clears through +0x38, notifies through +0x2C, and uses flag +0xE4 to invert the toggle comparison.

fields.name: ValueAccessorVTableSlot
fields.type_guess: vtable slot (+0xAC, value pointer accessor / toggle target)

classes.name: ScrollContainer
classes.responsibility: UI scroll container: stores a scroll offset at +0xE0, clamps it against position and extent obtained from vtable slots +0x18 and +0x20, and exposes a virtual accessor at slot +0xA8. A trivial setter writes +0xE0. Ownership DERIVED from existing analysis (scroll interpretation unproven by this packet alone).

classes.name: ListLayoutIndexer
classes.responsibility: Converts a screen y-coordinate into a list item index from layout fields (vertical bounds +0x4/+0x8, total item count +0x94, column offset +0x134, horizontal offset +0x13C, scroll offset +0x14C, item height +0x158, visible count +0x164) using CRTFtol truncation and clamping. Field roles mostly DERIVED from existing analysis; the formula itself is directly evidenced.

classes.name: TextBoxEditWidget
classes.responsibility: UI text edit-box object: string buffer pointer at +0x2F0, cursor/position pointer at +0x2F4, buffer size +0x2F8 (set to 256), character limit +0x300 (16), length/counter +0x2E8, and byte flags at +0xE0..0xE5, +0x1E7 and +0x2EC; buffer-set notification dispatched through vtable slot +0xA8. Exact flag semantics inferred from the edit-box interpretation in existing analysis.

fields.name: Flag1E7
fields.type_guess: byte (alternate buffer first byte / behavior flag)

classes.name: UIWidgetForwardWrapper
classes.responsibility: Thin UI widget wrappers: a forwarding shim that reads the DWORD at +0x0 and forwards to a widget-visibility toggle with reordered arguments, and an active/focus toggle that dispatches vtable slot +0xAC. The shim's target UIWidgetVisibilityToggle is not in the packet callee list, so its behavior is unproven.

fields.name: TypeOrVTableDword
fields.type_guess: dword (vtable or type id, passed to visibility toggle)

transitions.trigger: validated dispatch sets handler state to 1 via sub_487260(this, 1)

interfaces.name: UIValueStateAccessor
interfaces.purpose: Virtual slots on the UI dispatch-control object that validated dispatch handlers and the toggle helper rely on: +0x98 secondary validation, +0xAC value pointer accessor/toggle target, +0x38 set/clear, +0x2C notify.

interfaces.name: UIScrollMetricsAccessor
interfaces.purpose: Virtual slots on the scroll container consulted to clamp its stored offset: +0x18 position accessor, +0x20 extent accessor, +0xA8 result accessor (tail call).

compatibility_contracts.name: ScalarDeletingDestructorABI
compatibility_contracts.description: Scalar-deleting destructors take a char flag; when bit 0 is set they must deallocate this (FreeWrapper_7bcf) and return this, otherwise memory is retained (embedded or member object). A replacement executable must reproduce this convention on every object that exposes one of these stubs.

compatibility_contracts.name: SharedGlobal_8AB6EC_Protocol
compatibility_contracts.description: Global dword_8AB6EC is shared by collision-system helpers: Delegation (0x004B9CE0) must run before VehicleLifetimeAverageAccessor (0x004B9CB0) reads the lifetime average; RangeWidthGetter (0x004B9C80) receives the global's address via the thunk; and CollisionSystemInit (0x0047C960) is reached with a computed float argument. A replacement must preserve this sequence and the global's lifetime-average/range-width role.

compatibility_contracts.name: VTableSlotOffsets_UIObjects
compatibility_contracts.description: UI dispatch controls rely on fixed vtable slot offsets: +0x98 secondary validation, +0xAC value pointer accessor/toggle target, +0x38 set/clear, +0x2C notify, +0x18 position and +0x20 extent on the scroll container, and +0xA8 buffer-set notification / result accessor. A replacement object graph must keep these slot offsets stable.

compatibility_contracts.name: TextEditBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Text edit object layout: buffer pointer at +0x2F0, cursor pointer at +0x2F4, buffer size +0x2F8 (256), character limit +0x300 (16), length/counter +0x2E8, and byte flags at +0xE0..0xE5, +0x1E7, +0x2EC; buffer init stores pointer and size then notifies through vtable slot +0xA8.

compatibility_contracts.name: ListLayoutIndexFormula
compatibility_contracts.description: Screen y-coordinate to list item index: index = trunc((a2 - this[0x13C] - this[0x134] - this[0x4]) / this[0x158]) + this[0x14C] via CRTFtol, clamped up to scroll offset and (when a3 set) down to visible-page and total-item-count bounds; returns -1 when item height <= 0 or a2 outside [this[0x4], this[0x8]].

compatibility_contracts.name: InitFromDataBlockFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x0047EE5C copies a 36-byte block from global unk_7D0A30, formats an integer using the '%d' format string at global 0x005C3280 through the buffer-overflow-checked formatter, and conditionally dispatches the formatted buffer via ConditionalCallWrapper (0x0047E940). A replacement must preserve this copy-format-dispatch sequence and the trigger semantics internal to ConditionalCallWrapper.

unresolved: Object owners are mostly UNKNOWN (trust UNKNOWN in the packet); class groupings are pattern-based GUESS proposals and are not common-ownership proofs. In particular the eleven scalar-deleting destructors each install a distinct vtable constant and are grouped only by shared shape.
The shared cleanup helper sub_485EB0 is invoked by many fragments, but whether it continues construction or performs teardown is unresolved; it is identified only by the raw-source name.
The three vtable-reset fragments install distinct vtables (off_5AB968, off_5ABAC8, off_5ABC28); their relationship to the scalar-deleting destructors' base-class chain is unresolved.
Field semantics for most offsets (dispatch flags, list fields at +0x168/+0x16C/+0x170, layout fields, edit-box flags) are DERIVED/GUESS from existing analysis and not runtime-proven.

UIValueValidator, ConditionalCallWrapper and the widget-visibility toggle behavior are internal to their callees and not evidenced in this packet; the toggle target UIWidgetVisibilityToggle is not in the packet callee list.
In 0x00487D70 the decompiler local used for change detection is uninitialized in the raw source, so the exact trigger condition for the state-set branch cannot be determined.
The relationship between the extractor's node bases *(this+0xE4) / *(this+0xE8) and the traversal cursor in 0x00486600 / 0x00486630 is unproven.
0x0047EE5C has no recorded callers; the meaning of the 36-byte unk_7D0A30 data block and the parsed integer is unresolved.
Base destructor sub_495300 (chained from 0x0047F3F0) and its contract are outside this packet.
The float interpretation of constructor parameter 1065353216 (1.0) in 0x0047C910 comes from skeleton prose only.
Whether the deliberate truncation of the double argument to float in 0x0047C940 is intentional precision loss or a decompiler artifact is unknown.
The scroll/list-layout interpretation of the 0x00488970 / 0x00489F40 objects is DERIVED from existing analysis and unverified.
